{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study proposes a Bayesian approach to toxicological testing, discussing predictive power and using cardiac arrhythmia prediction as an example. It quantifies the relationship between test characteristics and predictive power, which is a measure of agreement between test results (animal model surrogate) and actual toxicity (human outcome).",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Testing for toxicities is an important activity in drug development.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "we use as examples tests available for the prediction of a substance's liability to cause the cardiac arrhythmia torsade de pointes.",
  "model_type": "in-vitro-or-in-silico-comparator",
  "model_evidence": "The proposed approach is easily implemented deterministically since values of the discriminatory power of the tests are readily and publicly available.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study discusses general principles of toxicological testing and predictive power, not specific animal species.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "A test's discriminatory power is characterized by its sensitivity and specificity... The investigator is, however, more interested in a test's predictive power"
}
